description: Srbijavode, the Serbian public water management company, publishes flood hazard and flood risk maps for the significant flood areas identified in the 2019 preliminary flood risk assessment of the Republic of Serbia. Hazard maps show flood extent for different return periods and classes of water depth; risk maps show the possible harm to people, the environment, cultural heritage and economic activity. The page lists each significant flood area by watercourse (for example the Danube from the Bulgarian border to the Đerdap 2 dam, the Timok and its branches, the Jasenica) with ZIP downloads of the hazard and risk maps, marking those still being prepared. The maps come from three projects of different dates and data quality: the Danube FloodRisk project of the ICPDR (2012 atlases at 1:100,000), SoFPAS phase 1 (2010 to 2012, EU IPA 2007) and the IPA 2014 flood recovery programme with the World Bank. Access is free by download; no licence is stated. Caveats: the page says the maps were made for flood risk management planning and are not meant for other uses, some areas are still in preparation, and the page is in Serbian. Coverage is Serbia; the page says the maps are also shown on the portals of the Republic Water Directorate and Vode Vojvodine. It supports flood exposure analysis of settlements, roads, bridges and utilities; related records are the Bulgarian flood hazard and risk maps and the FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer.
